criteria_notes.note: test_body_over_limit (413, text/plain, 'Content Too Large'); test_response_already_started_sends_no_second_response (receive returns http.disconnect, later sends dropped); test_client_disconnect_after_limit_is_swallowed; test_client_disconnect_without_limit_propagates. tests/test_body_limit.py::test_response_started_before_limit_is_not_followed_by_second_response covers the same at app level.

test_declared_content_length_is_rejected_before_body_is_read; test_declared_content_length_fails_fast; test_declared_content_length_replaces_response_of_app_that_never_reads (new, send() path); test_understated_content_length_is_enforced; test_invalid_content_length_is_ignored; test_non_ascii_digit_content_length_is_ignored (new). tests/test_body_limit.py::test_application_limit_applies_before_routing also covers a declared length on a 404 path.
tests/test_body_limit.py: test_default_is_unlimited, test_application_limit, test_router_limit, test_mount_limit, test_route_limit.

tests/test_body_limit.py: test_application_limit_applies_before_routing, test_inner_limits_raise_outer_limit and test_inner_limits_lower_outer_limit (route, mount and router, with Content-Length and chunked bodies). tests/middleware/test_body_limit.py::test_nested_middleware_overrides_limit.

tests/test_body_limit.py: test_multipart_overhead_counts_toward_limit (limit one byte under the full body size gives 413) and test_multipart_temp_files_closed_when_limit_is_crossed (multi-chunk raw ASGI, temp file closed). tests/test_formparsers.py::test_multipart_closes_tempfile_on_any_interruption (RuntimeError mid-parse closes the file).
Documented in docs/middleware.md (RequestBodyLimitMiddleware section), docs/applications.md and docs/routing.md (both 'Limiting the request body size'). No test; docs only.

summary: Both review findings are fixed and the three test files pass (156 passed). A Content-Length with non-ASCII digits, such as latin-1 b'\xb2', is now ignored instead of raising ValueError (`isascii()` added before `isdigit()` in `declared_too_large`). The send() path is now tested: an app that never calls receive(), with a declared Content-Length over the limit, gets its response replaced by the 413. I did not run the rest of the suite or any lint/type checks.
